body:
Two people shopping together from one shared list should see each other's picks
without either of them having to do anything — so neither buys the milk twice.

Two parts: sync fast enough while it matters, and make the change VISIBLE when
it lands. The second is the one that actually solves double-picking; a change
that arrives in 200 ms and is not noticed is no better than one that arrives in
a minute.

## Part 1 — 5-second sync for an opened list while the app is active

Poll every **5 s** when, and only when:

- **web**: the document is visible AND a list screen is open;
- **android**: the app is foregrounded AND a list screen is resumed.

Everything else stays exactly as it is: the web 100 s visible-tab fallback, the
Android 15-minute WorkManager job, plus the existing visibilitychange / online /
after-edit triggers. The 5 s loop is an addition scoped to "a list is on screen
and someone is looking at it", not a replacement for any of them.

Notes for whoever implements it:

- Must not stack with the existing timers. Web already has an in-flight guard
  (`inFlightRef` in useSync) — reuse it, and make sure the 100 s interval and the
  5 s interval cannot both fire a sync.
- Android: this is an in-process, lifecycle-aware coroutine in the list
  ViewModel, NOT a WorkManager job. WorkManager's floor is 15 minutes and it is
  the wrong tool for a foreground loop; it stays responsible for background sync.
- Stop on background/screen-close, not just on navigation, or a backgrounded app
  keeps polling.
- The WRITE side already behaves: Android's after-edit one-shot and the web's
  push() both go out immediately, so only the read side lags today.

### Why polling and not a server push

Measured on this Pi, 60-item list: an already-up-to-date `POST /sync` costs
**3.66 ms**, and a bare `SELECT change_seq` 0.019 ms. Two shoppers polling every
5 s is well under 0.25 % of one core. Polling is simply cheap enough.

SSE / WebSocket was considered and rejected, not deferred for lack of time. A
held connection occupies a WSGI worker for its whole life, and this server is a
Flask blueprint mounted in someone else's host app — server/README.md is
deliberately silent about the WSGI server, and the blueprint cannot dictate the
worker class. Under gunicorn's DEFAULT sync workers, every connected shopper
permanently consumes one; a handful of families shopping at once makes the whole
instance unreachable, including the web client and the APK download. It would
fail in the field and never in testing, because nobody tests with nine
simultaneous clients. Shipping it safely would mean a third mandatory deployment
requirement ("you must run threaded or async workers"), which is the same class
of footgun as the fail-open HMAC key T-122 removed.

Revisit only if 5 s proves insufficient in real use — and if so, with a hard cap
on concurrent connections and the worker-class requirement documented.

## Part 2 — quick animation when an item is checked off

When an item's status becomes `checked`:

1. **strike the name through** — fast;
2. then, **only if "show checked" is OFF**, the row slides out and collapses.

Both steps quick — this is a confirmation, not a performance. Something in the
region of 120 ms for the strike-through and 150 ms for the slide is the intent;
tune by feel, but err short. It fires on every check-off, not only a
collaborator's: a special case for "someone else did it" would make your own
taps behave differently from theirs, which is worse than no distinction at all.
`last_touched_by` is already on the wire (T-64) if a further collaborator-only
cue is ever wanted.

When **"show checked" is ON**: strike-through only. The row stays where it is —
sliding it away would contradict the setting.

Details worth getting right:

- **Direction follows the writing direction (T-126).** "Out to the left" is
  correct in LTR and wrong in Arabic; the row should exit toward the inline
  start, so it mirrors with the layout. Use the logical direction, not a
  hardcoded left.
- **Respect reduced motion**: `prefers-reduced-motion` on web, and the animator
  duration scale on Android. Both should degrade to an instant state change
  rather than a slow one.
- The row must not be interactable mid-animation, or a fast double-tap toggles
  something that is on its way out.
- Unchecking should be visually coherent with this, not a separate idiom.

## Verification

- Two clients on one list: check an item on A; it strikes and slides on B within
  ~5 s, unattended.
- Backgrounding either client stops its 5 s poll (assert no requests while
  backgrounded, not just that it "seems" idle).
- With "show checked" on, the row strikes through and stays put.
- Under RTL, the row exits toward the correct side.
- Under reduced motion, the change is instant and still visible.
title: live co-shopping: 5s sync for an open list, plus a quick check-off animation
